title: Emergency Supplies Checklist
lines: Sample content written for Lastbook Ark, based on public guidance from Ready.gov (US Federal Emergency Management Agency). Check current official guidance for your area.
A basic emergency supply kit helps a household get through the first days after a disaster, when power, water and shops may not be available.
Water: one gallon of water per person per day for at least three days, for drinking and sanitation.
Food: at least a three-day supply of non-perishable food, and a manual can opener.
Light and information: a flashlight, a battery-powered or hand-crank radio, and extra batteries.
First aid kit, a whistle to signal for help, and a dust mask to help filter contaminated air.

title: More Items for the Kit
lines: Moist towelettes, garbage bags and plastic ties for personal sanitation.
A wrench or pliers to turn off utilities such as gas and water.
Local maps printed on paper, because phones and the internet may not work.
A cell phone with chargers and a backup battery.
Prescription medicines and glasses, infant formula and diapers, and pet food and water, if your household needs them.
Copies of important family documents in a waterproof container.

title: Maintaining Your Kit
lines: Keep canned food in a cool, dry place. Store boxed food in tightly closed plastic or metal containers to protect it from pests.
Replace expired items as needed, and replace stored tap water every six months.
Re-think your needs every year and update your kit as your family's needs change.
Keep a kit at home, a smaller kit at work, and a kit in your car, because you may not be at home when an emergency happens.
